title: When is the sum of two multiples of three a multiple of six?
description: Multiples of three are put in rows of six, where some fill the rows exactly and some leave three over. Adding two of the same kind gives a multiple of six, and adding two of different kinds does not, which is checked with examples. The method is the same as the examples in the book on adding even numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: a multiple of three leaves either nothing or three when put in rows of six, and two leftovers of three make one more full row. Watch for students who think the sum of any two multiples of three must be a multiple of six.

video_script.why: A learner puts multiples of three in rows of six, adds the two kinds, and finds when the sum is a multiple of six.
video_script.substitution: the book's own idea: two multiples of three, and a sum that is a multiple of six
video_script.anchor: dots in rows of six, with the dots left over set apart, in the way the book uses rows of four
video_script.payoff_line: The sum is a multiple of six when both are the same kind of multiple of three. One of each kind gives an odd multiple of three.

final_answer.value: The sum is a multiple of 6 when both are odd multiples of 3 or both are even multiples of 3; one of each gives an odd multiple of 3
final_answer.spoken: the sum is a multiple of six when both are odd multiples of three or both are even multiples of three, and one of each kind gives an odd multiple of three

hold_back: The sum is a multiple of 6 when both are odd multiples of 3 or both are even multiples of 3; one of each gives an odd multiple of 3
maths_rules: multiples of 3 in rows of 6: even ones 6, 12 are 6m (nothing left); odd ones 3, 9 are 6m + 3 (three left)
6m + (6n + 3) = 6(m + n) + 3, three left over, an odd multiple of 3, not a multiple of 6
video_script.design: One idea: put multiples of three in rows of six and see what is left. Assumes the examples with rows of four. The dot rows stay on the board and the leftover dots are set apart.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about adding two multiples of three.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We will solve it the same way as the examples in your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>When is the sum a multiple of six, and when is it not?

beats.on_screen: the two blocks of dots stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: dots in rows of six: 6 and 12 fill the rows; 3 and 9 leave three dots apart

marks.even: six and twelve fill rows of six exactly
marks.odd: three and nine leave three dots apart

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Put multiples of three in rows of six. The even ones, like six and twelve, fill the rows exactly.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>The odd ones, like three and nine, leave three dots over.

beats.on_screen: Given: two multiples of 3, added together

marks.given: the two multiples of three and the plus sign are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are two multiples of three, and we add them.

beats.on_screen: To find: when the sum is a multiple of 6, when it is not, and the pattern
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find when the sum is a multiple of six. We also find when it is not.

beats.on_screen: even multiple of 3: 6m. Odd multiple of 3: 6m + 3

marks.even: the even kind is written as six m, full rows only
marks.odd: the odd kind is written as six m plus three, with three dots apart

narration: <bookmark mark='even'/>Step one, write the two kinds. An even multiple of three is six m, which is m full rows of six.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>An odd multiple of three is six m plus three, which is m full rows and three over.

marks.add: the full rows of both join into m plus n rows
marks.mult: the sum is a multiple of six

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add two even ones. Six m plus six n is six times m plus n.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>That is a multiple of six.

marks.left: the two leftovers of three sit together as six dots
marks.row: the six dots become one more full row

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, add two odd ones. The two leftovers of three make six.
<bookmark mark='row'/>Six is one more full row, so the sum is six times m plus n plus one. That is a multiple of six.

marks.mixed: the full rows join and three dots stay apart
marks.not: three dots cannot fill a row of six, so it is not a multiple of six

narration: <bookmark mark='mixed'/>Step four, add one of each. Six m plus six n plus three is six times m plus n, plus three.
<bookmark mark='not'/>Three dots cannot fill a row of six, so this sum is not a multiple of six. It is an odd multiple of three.

marks.odds: three plus nine shows twelve, two full rows
marks.evens: six plus twelve shows eighteen, three full rows
marks.mix: three plus six shows nine, one row and three over

narration: <bookmark mark='odds'/>Step five, put examples back. Three plus nine is twelve, which is six times two.
<bookmark mark='evens'/>Six plus twelve is eighteen, which is six times three.
<bookmark mark='mix'/>Three plus six is nine, which is six plus three. It leaves three over.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The sum is a multiple of 6 when both are odd multiples of 3 or both are even multiples of 3; one of each gives an odd multiple of 3

marks.kind: the words both odd and both even glow

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum is a multiple of six when both are the same kind of multiple of three. One of each kind gives an odd multiple of three.
<bookmark mark='kind'/>The same kind means both odd or both even.
